description:
GOAL

Make it possible for a library function to construct a tuple whose arity is known only at runtime, so Enum.zip/1 can return the Elixir-shaped tuple for any finite collection of enumerables.

CURRENT SIGNAL

Enum.zip/1 must transpose a collection and turn each row into a tuple whose arity equals the number of input enumerables. fz tuple literals have a source-known arity. There is no List.to_tuple/1, Tuple module, tuple constructor extern, or other library surface for a list to become a tuple. The compiler IR represents tuple construction as MakeTuple(Vec<Var>), and AOT registers tuple schemas by walking source-known tuple arities. Returning row lists instead would be an incompatible API, and hard-coding a few arities would only hide the missing capability.

STRATEGY

Trace tuple construction from source lowering through tuple schema registration, heap layout, GC, comparison, rendering, and field projection. Add one runtime-sized construction authority whose output remains an ordinary tuple to every existing consumer. Expose it through the narrowest honest standard-library API, then implement Enum.zip/1 by transposing rows and using that API. Reuse the existing tuple schema and AnyValue representation; do not introduce a second tuple kind.

ACCEPTANCE

- A list can be converted to ordinary tuples at multiple runtime-selected arities, including zero, two, and three.
- Constructed tuples render, compare, pattern-match, survive GC, and expose fields exactly like tuple literals.
- Enum.zip/1 matches Elixir for zero, two, and three input enumerables and stops at the shortest input.
- Tests cover interp, JIT, and AOT; full gates are green with warnings denied.
- Any temporary tuple-registration or test scaffolding is removed.
title: Enum.zip/1 needs runtime-sized tuple construction
